public_rationale: OpenAI reportedly ran a $9.3B operating loss in Q1 2026 on $5.7B revenue, which fits 'running this stuff at a loss'. On agents: GitHub ended flat Copilot pricing because hours-long agent sessions cost far more to serve than chat queries at the same price. Anthropic capped round-the-clock Claude Code use because it was costly. Both support the claim that agents widen losses under flat pricing. One counterpoint: OpenAI's gross margin rose from 33% to 39%, so company-wide figures do not clearly show agents deepening losses. On the plain reading (losses overall, bigger losses from agent users), the claim is supported.
limitations: 'Even bigger loss' is backed by provider statements and pricing changes, not measured loss data on agents.
OpenAI's improving gross margin points the other way at the company level.

statement.excerpt: And it’s this trade-off because basically they’ve been running this stuff at a loss. And with the agents come along, it’s an even bigger loss.

from_speaker: they've been running this stuff at a loss

our_interpretation: Plain reading: leading LLM providers (such as OpenAI and Anthropic, and resellers like GitHub Copilot) lose money serving their AI products, and agent use, especially under flat subscription pricing, costs them more than chat and so deepens those losses.
No period was named. I used 2025 (when coding agents spread) through the post date, with OpenAI's Q1 2026 results as the latest reported quarter.
Since he cites no figures, I treat the basis as press-reported estimates.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports show major LLM providers running operating losses, and provider statements or actions show agent use costs them much more than chat under existing pricing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible reports show the providers are profitable on serving their AI products, or that agent use does not raise their costs relative to what users pay.

evidence.explanation: OpenAI, the largest LLM provider, ran a $9.3B operating loss in Q1 2026 on $5.7B revenue. This supports 'running this stuff at a loss'.

evidence.excerpt: a short chat query and an autonomous coding session of several hours cost the end user the same, while the actual cost differs significantly.
evidence.explanation: GitHub's reasoning for ending flat pricing: agent sessions cost far more to serve than chat at the same price. This supports agents widening the gap between cost and revenue.

evidence.excerpt: the instances of non-stop use are also financially expensive for Anthropic.
evidence.explanation: Anthropic limited heavy agent (Claude Code) use under flat subscriptions because it was costly, consistent with agents deepening losses.

evidence.excerpt: Gross margin did climb from 33 to 39 percent.
evidence.explanation: OpenAI's gross margin improved year over year while agent use grew. This suggests that, company-wide, serving costs did not outrun revenue, which cuts against agents making losses 'even bigger' at that level.
